title: feat(accounts): moe-account-lease.mjs vm-credential derives a claude VM seat's job credential from the leased account's host sign-in, renewed only by the host's own claude (slice A of task-a200486f)
description:
Slice A of task-a200486f. The human's directive (2026-11-05, about 18:20Z): VM seats use the rotation accounts' existing subscription sign-ins automatically, as host and WSL seats do, with no manual `accounts vm-token` mint. This slice changes the helper only. The wrappers switch to it in slice B, and the docs follow in task-a200486f.

Today `vm-credential <id>` prints only a minted token from `<accounts dir>/claude-vm-tokens/<id>.token`.

Add to scripts/moe-account-lease.mjs:
- `vm-credential <id> <configDir> <claude command...>`: the minted token when one is stored (it still wins). Otherwise the access token of the account's own host sign-in: `claudeAiOauth.accessToken` in `<configDir>/.credentials.json`, which must have the VM_TOKEN_RE shape, a numeric `expiresAt` (ms) and `scopes` containing `user:inference`. It goes to stdout with no newline, exit 0. On failure: empty stdout, ONE stderr line `MOE_VM_CREDENTIAL_UNAVAILABLE reason=<reason>`, exit 3.
- `vm-credential-state <id> <configDir> <claude command...>`: the same resolution, but it never prints a credential. One stdout line, exit 0: `minted`, `signin<TAB><expiresAt as ISO 8601 UTC>` or `unavailable<TAB><reason>`. Missing arguments exit 2.
- Reasons, exported as VM_CREDENTIAL_REASONS:
  - `no-signin-file`: the folder or file is missing, not a regular file, a symlink, over 64 KiB or unreadable, or configDir's last segment is not the id.
  - `signed-out`: unparseable JSON, no claudeAiOauth, a token of another shape, a non-numeric expiresAt, or scopes without user:inference.
  - `expired`: renewal was needed and still left 5 minutes or less.
  - `no-claude`: renewal was needed but the claude command words cannot be run (probeCommand's rules).
- The one-argument `vm-credential <id>` form stays byte-for-byte as today (MOE_VM_TOKEN_UNAVAILABLE, exit 3).

Renewal follows claude's own rule. claude 2.1.318 renews when now + 300000 >= expiresAt (its Ex() function). Only then does the helper run the host's claude ONCE under CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=<configDir>, so claude refreshes its own sign-in under its own cross-process refresh lock, just as when a host seat starts on that account. Then the helper re-reads the file once.
- The run: the probe's command words plus `-p --model haiku --no-session-persistence --strict-mcp-config --tools ""`, a constant prompt on stdin, cwd os.tmpdir(), stdout and stderr discarded, and the probe's 60 s timeout.
- Its env is accountEnv(...) minus every MOE_* variable and CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_DIRS.
- Verified 2026-11-05 against an empty config folder: claude 2.1.318 (WSL claude, Windows claude.exe, and the npm claude.cmd through cmd.exe) answers "Not logged in", and an unknown flag answers "error: unknown option".
- Moe never uses, prints or passes the refresh token. It never writes .credentials.json and never calls the OAuth endpoint itself, so it cannot race a host seat's refresh.

Isolation stays as decisions 4 and 5 on task-1a8f1d0e set it: the renewable sign-in never leaves the host, and at most the short-lived access token goes to stdout, for the wrapper's job-frame pipe. This read-only use supersedes the 2026-10-26 sign-off's ".credentials.json is never opened" (human directive 2026-11-05). The helper header, the docs/SCHEMA.md claude-accounts entry and the registry.ts comments must say so, and scripts/tests/account-trust-docs.test.mjs pins it.

Out of scope:
- Both wrappers (slice B).
- The other docs (task-a200486f).
- macOS Keychain sign-ins: there is no file, so the result is `no-signin-file`, and a minted token stays the macOS route.
definitionOfDone: With no minted token, `vm-credential <id> <configDir> <claude…>` prints exactly the sign-in's access token (no newline, exit 0) when it has more than 5 minutes left, and runs no claude. A stored minted token still wins, and `vm-credential-state` then prints `minted`. The existing one-argument vm-credential test passes unchanged. Tested in scripts/tests/moe-account-lease.test.mjs.

A token with 5 minutes or less left is renewed by exactly one host claude run, then re-read. The test asserts the run's argv, its stdin prompt, a cwd outside the account folder, CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR = the folder, and an env with no TOKEN_ENV, PROVIDER_ENV, MOE_* or CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_DIRS. The helper never writes .credentials.json: bytes and mtime are unchanged when no renewal runs, and after one the file is exactly claude's own write. Tested with a fake claude.

Each failure cause in the description exits 3 with empty stdout and one stderr line `MOE_VM_CREDENTIAL_UNAVAILABLE reason=<r>`, and `vm-credential-state` prints `unavailable<TAB><r>`. There is one test row per cause: no-signin-file, signed-out, expired (claude fails or writes nothing) and no-claude.

No credential value appears anywhere but the fetch's stdout. Across every row, `vm-credential-state` stdout and both commands' stderr contain none of the access-token, renewed-token or refresh-token canaries, and the fetch's stdout never contains the refresh token. Tested.

The helper header, the docs/SCHEMA.md claude-accounts entry and the packages/moe-daemon/src/accounts/registry.ts comments (comment-only edits) state the read-only .credentials.json exception. scripts/tests/account-trust-docs.test.mjs pins it.
`node --test scripts/tests/moe-account-lease.test.mjs scripts/tests/account-trust-docs.test.mjs` passes on Linux node and on Windows node.exe.
taskRails: Tests and evidence use temp folders and a fake claude only. Never read, print or modify a real account's .credentials.json, and never run claude against a real account folder. An empty throwaway config folder is fine.
No credential value (an access or refresh token) in any log, task comment, chat message or test output.

implementationPlan.description:
Read the account's sign-in, read-only, with its tests (scripts/moe-account-lease.mjs, next to readVmCredential; edit with this seat's own editor, never a shell write).
- Export `VM_CREDENTIAL_REASONS = Object.freeze(['no-signin-file', 'signed-out', 'expired', 'no-claude'])`.
- Add the constants SIGNIN_FILE '.credentials.json', MAX_SIGNIN_BYTES 65536 and RENEW_MARGIN_MS 300000. Comment: claude 2.1.318 renews its sign-in when now + 300000 >= expiresAt (its bundled Ex()); task-docs read this exported list.
- Export `readSignInCredential(configDir, id)`. It returns `{ token, expiresAt }` or `{ reason }`, never throws, and never returns or keeps anything else from the file.
  - `no-signin-file` unless all hold: ACCOUNT_ID_RE.test(id); configDir is a non-empty string; path.basename(path.resolve(configDir)) === id; lstat(configDir).isDirectory(); lstat(<configDir>/.credentials.json).isFile(). Then open with O_RDONLY | (O_NOFOLLOW ?? 0), fstat isFile and size <= MAX_SIGNIN_BYTES, read, and close in finally: readVmCredential's pattern. Any IO error is no-signin-file.
  - `signed-out` unless JSON.parse succeeds and `claudeAiOauth` is an object whose accessToken matches VM_TOKEN_RE, whose expiresAt is a positive safe integer below 8.64e15 (a valid Date), and whose scopes is an array containing 'user:inference'.
  - Read-only: no write, chmod or utimes. Only accessToken and expiresAt leave the function; never the refresh token.
Tests in scripts/tests/moe-account-lease.test.mjs, in temp folders shaped like `<tmp>/claude-accounts/acct-1/.credentials.json`, never a real account. Use canaries ACCESS (sk-ant-oat01-…), REFRESH (sk-ant-ort01-…) and RENEWED.
- A valid file returns exactly { token: ACCESS, expiresAt }.
- One row per no-signin-file cause: missing folder; folder without the file; a folder named for another id; the file is a directory; a symlinked file (skip with a reason where symlinks need privileges, as the vm-credential test does); 65537 bytes.
- One row per signed-out cause: not JSON; {}; no accessToken; an sk-ant-api03 token; expiresAt as a string or 1e16; scopes without user:inference.
- Every row asserts the file's bytes and mtimeMs are unchanged and that no returned value contains REFRESH.
Error handling: every fs call sits in the existing try/finally shape; nothing here can throw to a caller.

Renewal through the host's own claude, the resolution and both commands, with their tests (same two files).
- Generalize probeCommand: export `claudeCommand(words, tail, env, platform, exists)` with probeCommand's exact rules:
  - a .js/.mjs/.cjs claude runs under this node;
  - on Windows, PATH x PATHEXT; an .exe/.com runs directly, a .cmd through cmd.exe, refusing any word with '"', '%', '!', CR or LF.
  probeCommand becomes `claudeCommand(words, ['auth', 'status', '--json'], …)`, and its existing tests stay unchanged.
- Export `RENEW_ARGS = ['-p', '--model', 'haiku', '--no-session-persistence', '--strict-mcp-config', '--tools', '']` and `RENEW_PROMPT` (a constant one-line prompt, e.g. 'Reply with OK.'). Comment: the empty last word disables every tool, and `--tools` is variadic, so the prompt goes on stdin, not as a positional. Verified 2026-11-05 against an empty CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR: WSL claude 2.1.318, Windows claude.exe and the npm claude.cmd through cmd.exe all answer 'Not logged in · Please run /login', and a bad flag answers 'error: unknown option'.
- Export `renewEnv(env, dir, platform)`: accountEnv(env, dir, platform) minus every name starting with MOE_ and CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_DIRS, case-insensitive on win32.
- Export `renewSignIn(configDir, words, env, platform)`:
  - plan = claudeCommand(words, RENEW_ARGS, …); null returns false.
  - spawnSync as probeSignIn does (shell for the cmd line) with input RENEW_PROMPT, stdio ['pipe','ignore','ignore'], cwd os.tmpdir(), windowsHide and PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS.
  - Return false only for ENOENT; otherwise true, whatever claude's exit or a timeout, because the re-read decides.
  - Never read claude's output.
- Export `resolveVmCredential(env, id, configDir, words, { now = Date.now, renew = renewSignIn } = {})`:
  - readVmCredential first: `{ source: 'minted', token }`.
  - Else readSignInCredential: a reason passes through.
  - expiresAt - now() > RENEW_MARGIN_MS gives `{ source: 'signin', token, expiresAt }`.
  - Else call renew once (false gives `{ reason: 'no-claude' }`) and re-read once (a reason passes through). Still within the margin gives `{ reason: 'expired' }`.
  - Moe itself never refreshes, never calls an OAuth endpoint and never writes the file. Claude's own refresh lock makes concurrent renewals by several seats safe.
- main():
  - `vm-credential <id>` alone stays byte-for-byte.
  - `vm-credential <id> <configDir> <words…>`: words are required, else usage and exit 2. On success, the token goes to stdout with no newline, exit 0. Otherwise one stderr line `MOE_VM_CREDENTIAL_UNAVAILABLE reason=<reason>`, exit 3.
  - `vm-credential-state <id> <configDir> <words…>`: missing arguments give usage and exit 2. Otherwise exit 0 with one line: `minted`, `signin\t<new Date(expiresAt).toISOString()>` or `unavailable\t<reason>`.
Tests:
- Add a fakeRenewClaude fixture, separate from fakeClaude, whose log shape the signin-state test pins with deepEqual.
  - It logs args, cwd, stdin, CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, and only the presence (never a value) of MOE_WORKER_ID, CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_DIRS, CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK.

Its args are the words' extra args plus RENEW_ARGS, stdin === RENEW_PROMPT, realpath(cwd) === realpath(os.tmpdir()), CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR is the folder, none of the five names is present (all five set in the helper's env), and the file's sha equals the fake's own write. A state call right after runs no claude.
  4. expired: the fake exits 1 writing nothing, or writes a token with 2 minutes left.
  5. no-claude: a missing .js claude path.
  6. The boundary through resolveVmCredential with an injected now and a stub renew: exactly 300000 ms left renews, 300001 does not.

- Every row asserts that no canary appears in state stdout/stderr or fetch stderr, and that fetch stdout never holds REFRESH. The existing one-argument vm-credential test passes unchanged.
Error handling: renewSignIn and resolveVmCredential never throw. main() keeps its single try/catch, and a usage error prints USAGE only.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
- Moe refreshing with the refresh token itself: rejected. Refresh tokens rotate, so a Moe refresh would race a host seat's and log it out. Claude already serializes refreshes across processes with a lockfile and adopts a sibling's result.
- Triggering renewal with `claude auth status`: rejected. It never refreshes; it reads local state only.
- A no-model trigger such as an unknown model name: rejected as fragile. A one-word haiku -p run costs almost nothing and is the stable contract ('any API call refreshes first').
- A larger start margin (e.g. 30 min) plus waiting: rejected. Claude refreshes only inside its own 5-minute window, so a larger margin means idle waits, and it still cannot cover long jobs.
- Taking configDir from the registry rule rather than from the wrapper: rejected. The wrapper already holds the lease's configDir, which the vm-route harness fakes as <home>/<id>. The basename check guards against wiring mistakes.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
- The helper is the wrappers' single account-side tool. They call it by subcommand and read the first stdout line: ps1 Invoke-MoeAccountHelper (stderr dropped; null on a nonzero exit), and sh `$("$NODE_CMD" "$ACCOUNT_HELPER" …)`.
- `vm-credential-state` must exit 0 so ps1 gets its line.
- The existing tests never run the real claude or touch a real config folder; keep it so.
- The smoke in checkRefs[0] runs the real claude only against an empty temp folder.
- From WSL, `env -i` needs a quoted "PATH=$PATH", because Windows entries contain spaces. node.exe gets the Windows environment, not WSL's, except WSLENV names.
planningNotes.risks:
- A future claude may move credentials out of .credentials.json (the binary mentions a storageV5). The read then fails closed (no-signin-file/signed-out), a minted token still works, and the smoke in the gate catches argv drift.
- If the server revokes the old access token on refresh, a running VM job sees a 401 early. That is the same failed-job route as expiry; slice B and the docs say so.
- The renewal run makes one tiny haiku request on the account. It counts toward usage negligibly. It runs only when the token has 5 minutes or less left, at most once per call.
- spawnSync's timeout kills cmd.exe on Windows but may leave claude.exe briefly. Claude's lock has dead-holder takeover, and the re-read decides.
- Clock: expiresAt was written by claude from the same host clock, so there is no skew between them.
